slots.jd.lattice-cloud.full:
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Lattice Cloud — Remote (US)

About the role
Lattice Cloud runs a multi-region container platform serving 1,200+ enterprise customers. The infrastructure team is hiring an SRE to own the reliability of our control plane: ingress, scheduling, and the metadata layer. You'll set SLOs, drive postmortem culture, and reduce on-call burden through deliberate engineering investment.

What you'll do
- Own incident response for the control plane: lead postmortems, identify systemic patterns, drive corrective actions to completion.
- Define and instrument SLOs and SLIs for our scheduling pipeline; partner with product engineering to fold reliability budgets into roadmap planning.
- Improve observability: extend our Prometheus/Grafana stack, add structured tracing where it's missing, write runbooks that cut MTTR.
- Author Terraform modules that codify infrastructure standards across teams; review IaC changes from product engineers.
- Participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation (one week in five). Mentor junior engineers on incident command.
- Run blameless postmortems and own the action-item tracker.

What we're looking for
- 4+ years operating production distributed systems at scale (preferably Kubernetes-based).
- Strong programming in at least one of: Python, Go.
- Hands-on experience with: Prometheus/Grafana, Terraform, AWS or GCP, structured logging, distributed tracing.
- Track record of leading incident response and writing postmortems other engineers actually read.
- Comfort with on-call as a craft, not a chore.

Nice to have
- Service mesh experience (Istio, Linkerd).
- Previous SRE-track promotion or staff-level scope.
- Open-source contributions to observability tools.

Compensation
$185–$225K base + equity. Full benefits, $2K/yr learning budget, fully remote with quarterly team gatherings.
slots.r1.b1: Owned reliability of the API edge for a B2B SaaS serving roughly 800 customer tenants on AWS EKS.
slots.r1.b2: Reduced control-plane error budget burn by tightening retry semantics in the ingress layer; rewrote the Envoy filter config and added a dashboard that on-call uses every shift.
slots.r1.b3: Authored Terraform modules for VPC peering and IAM role provisioning that the platform team adopted as the standard.
slots.r1.b4: Took on-call rotation roughly one week in four; led postmortems for two Sev-1 incidents and tracked action items to completion.
slots.r1.b5: Wrote a runbook library covering the top ten alert types; runbook usage cut MTTR for those alerts noticeably.
slots.r2.b1: Maintained the data ingestion pipeline (Kafka + Flink) for an analytics product used by internal sales teams.
slots.r2.b2: Migrated the monitoring stack from a SaaS APM to self-hosted Prometheus + Grafana, saving on the licensing line item and giving the team direct query access.
slots.r2.b3: Built a Slack bot in Python that posted incident timelines as they unfolded; on-call adopted it across the org.
slots.r2.b4: Mentored two interns through their first on-call shadow rotations.
slots.summary.1: Site Reliability Engineer with four years operating Kubernetes-based platforms in production. Strong incident-response habits and a preference for fixing systemic causes over patching symptoms. Comfortable in Python and Go.
slots.x4.b1: **kube-budget-cli** — open-source Go tool that reports namespace-level cost attribution from Kubernetes resource quotas. ~120 GitHub stars.
slots.x4.b2: Active reviewer on the Prometheus operator GitHub repo (12 merged PRs over 2024).
